summary: KJV quote and Christ-landing are clean, but Aaron's first-person claim to have driven the scapegoat into the desert contradicts Lev 16:21, where a fit man (not Aaron) leads it away.

findings.beat: Beat 2 — 'I laid my hands on its head, confessed every sin of the people over it, and drove it into the desert to be lost.'
findings.quote_or_claim: and drove it into the desert to be lost
findings.problem: The high priest did NOT personally drive/lead the scapegoat into the wilderness. Lev 16:21 says Aaron lays hands and confesses, then 'shall send him away by the hand of a fit man into the wilderness' — a designated fit man does the driving out. The first-person 'I... drove it into the desert' inverts who performed the act, the same class of fact-error flagged previously (the Lev 10 'I carried them out myself' inversion). Aaron's own actions were the laying-on of hands and confession; the sending-out was executed by the fit man.
findings.proposed_fix_text: The second I did not kill — I laid my hands on its head, confessed every sin of the people over it, and sent it away into the desert to be lost.
